findings.issue_text: Removing `float: right` from `.panel` breaks right alignment of the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header because `margin-left: auto` and `order` do not apply outside the flex `.contents` container
`-ms-align-items` is an invalid and ignored IE/Edge flexbox property; it should be removed because the correct legacy `-ms-flex-align` declaration is already emitted

goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

per_golden_matches.reasoning: Both comments identify the same core issue: removing `float: right` from `.panel` breaks the right alignment of the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header. The golden comment explains this is because `.panel` is nested inside `.row` and not a flex item, while the candidate explains it's because `margin-left: auto` and `order` don't apply outside the flex `.contents` container. Both are describing the same underlying problem - the flexbox-based alignment won't work for the non-flex context of the noscript header.
